pr_title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Fix backoff problem when quickly reverting resize patch
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

For container restarts as a result of resize patch, this PR reset backoff for corresponding container.

We need it to overcome slow reconcile ( range of 1-3 minutes) for this corner case. It will still wait for kubelet's next reconcile loop (interval is 1 minute)

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #125843

Fixes  #119838

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Please refer to issue #125205 for background information.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```
NONE
```

> It doesn't feel right to reset the backoff in computePodResizeAction. It also means the backoff doesn't get reset if the container is restarted before getting to computePodReszieAction. How about resetting the backoff in `handlePodResourcesResize` instead? And say we reset it whenever a container's allocated resources changes?
> 
> here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2824

issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Container resize policy feature introduced in v1.27 doesn't interrupt CrashLoopBackOff
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Hi, does someone know how to “break” the CrashLoopBackOff container status? I don’t want to wait all the backoff time nor delete the whole pod. I’m using the new features of restarting the container after resizing introduced in Kubernetes v1.27, but it seems that after I resize the container using the Python client, it still waits for the back-off time to finish before trying to run the container again.

Deployment info:

```spec:
      containers:
        - name: ...
          image: systemautoscaler/prime-numbers:dev
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          ports:
            - containerPort: ...
          resizePolicy:
            - resourceName: cpu
              restartPolicy: RestartContainer
            - resourceName: memory
              restartPolicy: RestartContainer
```

### What did you expect to happen?

No matter the state of the container, when I resize it, it should be restarted, even if waiting for Back Off.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a deployment with the spec field as specified above.
2. Scale down container resources to 1m CPU and to 1Mi memory (both limits and requests) using the Kubernetes API e.g. `kubernetes.client.CoreV1Api().patch_namespaced_pod(name=pod_name, namespace=namespace, body=new_pod_data)`
3. Wait till the container is in CrashLoopBackOff and then try to scale up the container resources with enough CPU and memory to run successfully.

### Anything else we need to know?
